skill.name: canvas-design
skill.description: Creates design-first visual philosophies and turns them into polished static PNG or PDF artwork with minimal text and local font assets.
skill.summary: Generate museum-style poster, art, and static canvas designs from a user brief.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static system-reconnaissance and backtick alerts are false positives from OFL license text and Markdown prose. Bundled TTF font binaries remain low-confidence confirmed findings because they were not statically inspectable. The skill also contains a user-intent spoofing instruction and an unbounded font download instruction that should be fixed before publication.

remediation.issue: User-intent spoofing in the skill prompt.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the statement that the user already requested perfection. Replace it with a neutral refinement step that respects the current user request.
Restrict the skill to bundled fonts by default. Require explicit user approval, trusted sources, and integrity checks for any new font downloads.

remediation.issue: Bundled binary font assets are not text-auditable.
remediation.suggestion: Publish font provenance, checksums, and source URLs. Add a manual asset review process before marketplace approval.

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The line explicitly asserts a user message that may not exist, creating untrusted context. It does not attempt credential theft, so high severity is sufficient.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded External Font Download Instruction

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction directly encourages downloading new font assets. The risk is contextual because downloads depend on the host agent and user environment.

content.value_statement: Static artwork prompts often produce generic layouts with too much text. This skill turns a brief into a visual philosophy, then a refined PNG or PDF design.
actual_capabilities: Creates a written design philosophy before generating the final artwork.
Builds single-page PNG or PDF visual artifacts with minimal text.
Uses bundled font assets from the canvas-fonts directory when appropriate.
Guides typography, composition, color, space, and visual hierarchy.
Supports multi-page visual sets when the user asks for them.
limitations: It depends on the host agent's ability to create image or PDF files.
It is not a legal review for fonts, trademarks, or copyrighted reference material.
It does not validate binary font files or downloaded font sources.
It may need extra user direction for exact brand, print, or accessibility requirements.

use_cases.title: Event Poster Exploration
use_cases.description: Designers can turn a loose venue, exhibit, or campaign brief into a polished poster direction.

use_cases.title: Editorial Visual Concept
use_cases.description: Writers and editors can create abstract cover art or page artwork for essays and zines.

use_cases.title: Brand Mood Artifact
use_cases.description: Founders can generate a visual mood piece that tests typography, color, and composition.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Poster
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a one-page PNG poster for [topic]. Use minimal text, strong composition, and a refined visual philosophy.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a static artwork.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a Visual Direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a PDF art piece for [subject]. Develop the design philosophy first, then express it with typography, color, and spatial rhythm.
prompt_templates.scenario: When the user wants a polished visual concept.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Multi-Page Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a three-page visual series for [theme]. Keep each page distinct, but connect them through one design philosophy.
prompt_templates.scenario: For campaigns, lookbooks, or presentation art.

prompt_templates.title: Refine an Existing Concept
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this concept: [brief]. Create a restrained, museum-quality PNG with subtle references, precise typography, and no crowded elements.
prompt_templates.scenario: For advanced users with a specific aesthetic target.

output_examples.input: A poster for an underground film night.
output_examples.output: A PDF poster concept with sparse venue text, dark geometric forms, and a manifesto describing the visual movement.

output_examples.input: Abstract art for a climate essay.
output_examples.output: A PNG artwork using layered measurement marks, restrained color, and minimal labels that hint at environmental change.

output_examples.input: A three-page lookbook for a ceramics studio.
output_examples.output: A small PDF series with varied page compositions, tactile color, and typography that supports the studio identity.

best_practices: Provide the subject, mood, output format, and any required text before generation.
Ask for local or approved fonts when font sourcing matters.
Review the generated design for copyright, brand, accessibility, and print constraints.
anti_patterns: Do not use it for text-heavy reports, slides, or documentation layouts.
Do not ask it to copy a living artist, brand, or protected work.
Do not allow unapproved downloads when working in a restricted environment.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates static visual artwork as PNG or PDF, plus a short design philosophy.

faq.question: Can it make multi-page designs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create several related pages when the user requests a series.

faq.question: Does it use fonts?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use bundled fonts in canvas-fonts, and it may request other fonts.

faq.question: Is it safe for brand work?
faq.answer: It can support concept work, but users should review trademarks, licenses, and brand rules.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I include in my prompt?
faq.answer: Include the subject, audience, format, required words, mood, and any font or color constraints.
